idiom_name: accessor property with a cached backing field (lazy getter)
implementation_notes: JavaScript defers via the getter: an accessor property computes on read, and memoization is the self-overwriting pattern MDN calls a smart / lazy getter - the first read builds the value and stores it, later reads return the stored one. MDN is explicit that getters are not lazy or memoized by nature, so the caching is written by hand, and a get trap on a Proxy object is the dynamic alternative when the member name is not known statically. The classic stand-in class is still justified when one object must present several methods or satisfy instanceof expectations, rather than exposing a single deferred property.
pitfalls: A lazy getter must not be used for a value expected to change, and null must be the only sentinel tested - a legitimately false or empty result stored in the backing field is indistinguishable from 'not built yet' unless you check for undefined or use a separate flag.
Class accessors live on the prototype, so the cached value has to be an own property of the instance; a shared closure variable would be cached once for every instance.

There is no single-flight guarantee: two concurrent async first accesses (or a re-entrant getter) can both start the expensive construction, because JavaScript gives no atomicity to the check-then-assign.
